```{r}
library("robis")
library("tidyverse")
library("ggplot2")
library("lubridate")
library("stringr")
library("dplyr")
library("sf")
library("here")
library("ggspatial")
library("prettymapr")
library("leaflet")


```
```{r}
#load gbr map
# Tell GDAL to automatically rebuild the missing .shx file
sf::sf_extSoftVersion()["GDAL"] # (Optional: just to confirm sf is using GDAL)
Sys.setenv(SHAPE_RESTORE_SHX = "YES")

# read shapefile and convert coordinate system to (WGS 84)
gbr_mpa <- sf::st_read("C:/Users/nrmou/OneDrive/Documents/TechniquesMS/Nudi/data/GBR_MPA.shp")

st_crs(gbr_mpa) <- 4326
```


```{r}
# Fetch sea turtle data within the GBR bounding box from OBIS
turtle_data <- robis::occurrence(
  scientificname = "Chelonia mydas", 
  geometry = "POLYGON ((142 -25, 142 -10, 154 -10, 154 -25, 142 -25))"
)

# Preview the columns to look for tracking identifiers
head(turtle_data)
```

```{r}
# 2. Clean data and locate individual tracking identifiers
# Telemetry datasets often store individual animal tags in 'individualID' or 'fieldNumber'.
turtles_clean <- turtle_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(decimalLatitude) & !is.na(decimalLongitude)) %>%
  # Fallback to identify individual animals if standard columns are missing
  mutate(individual_id = coalesce(organismID, fieldNumber, datasetID)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(individual_id))
```

```{r}
# 3. Identify the Top 5 individuals with the most tracking data points
top_5_turtles <- turtles_clean %>%
  count(individual_id, sort = TRUE) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 5) %>%
  pull(individual_id)
```

```{r}
# Filter the dataset to include only these 5 individuals
turtles_top5 <- turtles_clean %>%
  filter(individual_id %in% top_5_turtles) %>%
  # Arrange by time if date/time stamps are present to ensure lines connect chronologically
  arrange(individual_id, eventDate) 


```

```{r}
# 4. Convert tabular data to spatial objects (SF)
turtles_sf <- st_as_sf(
  turtles_top5, 
  coords = c("decimalLongitude", "decimalLatitude"), 
  crs = 4326
)

# Group points into paths (lines) for migration visualization
turtles_lines <- turtles_sf %>%
  group_by(individual_id) %>%
  summarize(do_union = FALSE) %>%
  st_cast("LINESTRING")

# Extract the bounding box of your turtle tracking data
bb <- st_bbox(turtles_lines)

```


```{r}
#make a graph showing the turtle mirgartion within the great barrier reef
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = gbr_mpa, fill = "lightblue", color = "darkblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = turtles_lines, aes(color = individual_id), size = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = turtles_sf, aes(color = individual_id), size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Turtle ID") +
  labs(title = "Green Sea Turtle Migration within the Great Barrier Reef",
       subtitle = "Tracking data for top 5 individuals",
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_minimal() +
  annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.2) +
  annotation_north_arrow(location = "tl", which_north = "true", 
                         style = north_arrow_fancy_orienteering()) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(bb["xmin"], bb["xmax"]), 
           ylim = c(bb["ymin"], bb["ymax"]), 
           expand = TRUE) # Set expand = TRUE to give a small natural margin around the data
```
```{r}
# Add a 10% buffer to longitude and latitude ranges
x_range <- bb["xmax"] - bb["xmin"]
y_range <- bb["ymax"] - bb["ymin"]
buffer <- 5.0

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = gbr_mpa, fill = "lightblue", color = "darkblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_sf(data = turtles_lines, aes(color = individual_id), size = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_sf(data = turtles_sf, aes(color = individual_id), size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Turtle ID") +
  labs(title = "Green Sea Turtle Migration within the Great Barrier Reef",
       subtitle = "Tracking data for top 5 individuals",
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_minimal() +
  annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.2) +
  annotation_north_arrow(location = "tl", which_north = "true", 
                         style = north_arrow_fancy_orienteering()) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(bb["xmin"] - (x_range * buffer), bb["xmax"] + (x_range * buffer)), 
           ylim = c(bb["ymin"] - (y_range * buffer), bb["ymax"] + (y_range * buffer)), 
           expand = FALSE)
```

```{r}
# 5. Build and plot the migration map
ggplot() +
  # Add a background map layer using OpenStreetMap or standard base maps
  annotation_map_tile(type = "osm", zoom = 6) +
  
  # Plot migration tracks as paths
  geom_sf(data = turtles_lines, aes(color = individual_id), size = 1, alpha = 0.8) +
  
  # Plot exact recorded locations as points
  geom_sf(data = turtles_sf, aes(color = individual_id), size = 1.5, alpha = 0.6) +
  
  # Map aesthetics and labels
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set1", name = "Turtle ID") +
  labs(
    title = "Migration Pathways of Top 5 Green Sea Turtles",
    subtitle = "Great Barrier Reef Region (Data sourced via robis)",
    x = "Longitude", 
    y = "Latitude"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  annotation_scale(location = "bl", width_hint = 0.2) +
  annotation_north_arrow(location = "tl", which_north = "true")
```


```{r}
turtles <- robis::occurrence(
  scientificname = "Chelonia mydas",
  startdate = "2000-01-01",
  enddate = "2025-12-31",
  fields = c("occurrenceID", "scientificName", "decimalLatitude", 
             "decimalLongitude", "individualCount", "eventDate")
)
```

```{r}
# Assuming 'turtles' is your loaded OBIS dataframe filtered for Chelonia mydas
turtles$year <- as.numeric(format(as.Date(turtles$eventDate), "%Y"))

# 1. Histogram of observations over time
ggplot(turtles, aes(x = year)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, fill = "forestgreen", color = "white") +
  labs(title = "Green Sea Turtle (*Chelonia mydas*) Records Over Time",
       x = "Year", y = "Observation Count") +
  theme_minimal()

# 2. Basic spatial scatter plot of coordinates
ggplot(turtles, aes(x = decimalLongitude, y = decimalLatitude)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, color = "darkgreen", size = 1) +
  coord_quickmap() +
  labs(title = "Green Sea Turtle Spatial Distribution",
       x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude") +
  theme_bw()
```
